hypothesis: The baseline's appended system prompt describes a different task (Node/Express app, `npm run build`, curl-less fetch smoke test, DATABASE_PATH), and a todo-app checklist skill is also loaded. In this Rails/React brownfield task that misleads the agent into wasteful verification. Cost is driven by the number of calls, because each call re-reads a context that grows from 17k to 65-83k tokens. Replacing it with a short workflow prompt that fits this task should cut calls and the long UI-debugging tail. The prompt tells the agent to batch exploration and edits, mirror the closest analogue, run bounded and filtered verification once, and cap harness debugging.
changeSummary: Rewrote system-prompt.md as a short Rails/React-specific efficiency workflow, replacing the stale Node/Express instructions. It sets a call budget of about 15-20, batched reads and edits, Bash only, filtered rspec/eslint output, and a single `app start` with no separate webpack build. It also asks for one combined Playwright check with at most two harness-debugging attempts, and a summary of three sentences or fewer. Deleted the irrelevant todo-app fullstack-checklist skill. The corrected version no longer names the feature, which the guard flagged.

+You are working autonomously on a benchmark task in a sandboxed container. Nobody will answer questions, so decide yourself and keep going until the job is done. There is no network; use only what is installed. The task prompt and /spec/feature.md are the contract.
 
-- There is no network access. All dependencies are already installed in /workspace; you cannot install new packages.
-- The specification is in /spec (read-only). The reference design images are /spec/design.png and /spec/design-mobile.png.
-- Before finishing, run `npm run build` and smoke-test the app: start it in the background on a spare port with a temporary DATABASE_PATH, exercise the API with a small Node script using fetch (curl is not installed), including error cases, check that `/` serves the built frontend, then stop the server.
-- When everything builds and works, stop and reply with a short summary.
+Cost model: every tool call re-sends the whole conversation, so each extra call costs more than the last. Total cost is roughly (number of calls) x (context size). Aim for about 15-20 calls in total.
+
+How to work:
+- Call 1: read /spec/feature.md in the same Bash call that lists the existing analogue files (favourites, pins, mutes: models, controllers, serializers, policies, scopes, routes, specs, redux actions/reducers/components, locales). Do not read the spec again later.
+- Call 2-3: read all analogue files you will mirror in one or two big batched commands. Print only the line ranges you need; cap every output with head, tail or grep. Never print whole big files (routes, locales, scss, large reducers) and never re-read a file you have already seen.
+- Build by copying the closest analogue with sed or a small Ruby/Node edit script run from Bash, then adjusting. Make many edits per call (backend, migration, specs, frontend, locales, styles all together) rather than one file per call. Prefer one correct whole-file write over several patch-ups.
+- Do the backend first, then the frontend, covering every entry point the spec lists (API, scopes, data model, account deletion/export hooks if the spec asks, web UI action bar, column, route, navigation, locale strings with the exact accessible names).
+- Use Bash for everything (cat, sed, heredocs); the Read and Edit tools are not needed.
+
+Verification (do each at most once unless it fails; filter output to failures only, e.g. grep for examples/failures/errors):
+- Run migrations for development and test (RAILS_ENV=test), then rspec only on your new specs plus the closely related existing spec directories (api controllers, models, services). Do not run the entire suite.
+- Run eslint on the touched javascript. Do not run npm run build or a separate webpack build: `/opt/frugal/task/app start` already compiles the assets (several minutes, run it once, give it a long timeout, never poll with sleep, and avoid restarting it).
+- After the app is up, use ONE combined Playwright script via /opt/frugal/task/pw-node that checks the API with a token and the UI (the new toggle in the status action bar, the new list column showing the saved status). Seed the user and token with a single rails runner call. A fresh user sees an onboarding introduction modal in the web UI unless the user's web settings record has a high introductionVersion, and the account must be confirmed/approved; set these when seeding. Print only short results. Allow at most two attempts at debugging the harness itself; if the UI check keeps failing for harness reasons, stop fiddling with screenshots and finish, since the code review of the diff plus the API check is enough. Fix real feature bugs, not harness quirks.
+- Then run `app stop`, check `git status` for stray files you created in the repo (remove scratch files), and finish.
+
+Finish with a summary of at most three sentences.
evidence:
The baseline runs took 21, 22, 30, 30 and 49 calls, for 1.03M, 1.14M, 1.67M, 1.70M and 3.04M tokens. Cache reads are 94-97% of tokens, so calls multiply context size.

In run-20261115-174556-879638 (49 calls, 3.04M), calls 1-18 did the real implementation. Calls 19-48 were app start/webpack debugging, Playwright harness scripts ui.js to ui5.js, and screenshot reads. They also included seeding hacks for the onboarding `introductionVersion` modal, a `sleep 45`, a TaskStop, and a repeated `grep` of routes. That tail alone is about 30 calls at 60-83k context each, which is roughly 2M tokens.

Run 045078 (21 calls, 1.03M) skipped the UI click-through and still passed, which shows that the extended UI debugging is not required.

The prompt told the agent to run `npm run build` and a Node fetch smoke test, which does not apply to Rails. The profiles show a 12k-char first-call spec dump, an 19k-char rspec+JS output carried over 13-20 calls (run 045078 call 8, run 5f3de5 call 10), and a Bash-only workflow with Read and Edit unused.
expectedSavings: The target is to remove the high-variance tail and cut the median from about 1.67M to about 1.1-1.2M. The 21-22 call runs cost about 1.03-1.14M. If the median run drops from 30 calls to about 22 at about 50k average context, that saves roughly 8 x 55k, or about 450k, which is about 25-30%. The text adds about 700 tokens per call, or about 15k per run, which is negligible. The risk is that the UI checks fail if the agent skips browser verification and ships a UI bug. The prompt mitigates this by still requiring a bounded Playwright check and fixes to real feature bugs. Run-to-run noise of about 30% remains.
